summary: Cross-cultural and engineering review (Müller-Römer 2008): no conclusive explanation for pyramid construction; argues perpendicular and spiral ramps are unlikely, proposes steep ramps parallel to core steps with winches.
content: Müller-Römer (2008): 'no conclusive explanation has been proposed so far' for Old Kingdom pyramid construction. Argues perpendicular and spiral ramps are not likely to have played a significant role, citing ramp volume, lack of archaeological evidence, and schedule problems. Proposes steep ramps erected parallel to the sides of the core steps, hauling material with winches (rollers), with a working platform for casing. Notes the Great Pyramid construction time frame is a maximum of 23 years. This is one more competing engineering hypothesis; the Inca at Ollantaytambo used ramps and slides, showing ramps were a common ancient technique, but the Egyptian method remains debated.
